decision: held: Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling asks for an outcome-scoped assessment of lower-body strength from the 2024 SR/MA, with no generic credit. That source, PMID 39514262 (Journal of Sports Sciences 2024, doi 10.1080/02640414.2024.2423578), is not in the record's references and has no legitimate free full text (OpenAlex closed, Semantic Scholar no openAccessPdf, Europe PMC subscription only). Its included trials, betaine doses, durations and dosage forms therefore cannot be verified, so no lower-body strength context can be approved and the PMID is not added to the record. The record is not downgraded to reference, so it is not marked as a categorical zero.
summary: Existing human research is retained: limited positive exercise results (2024 SR/MA lower-body strength; female body-fat trial; CrossFit repetitions), with other exercise outcomes null; this is an unfinished outcome-scoped assessment, not a zero. The 2024 SR/MA abstract (39514262) reports 17 placebo-controlled studies, 317 healthy participants aged 15-60 (21% female), chronic betaine for at least 7 days: maximal strength SMD 0.47 (95% CI 0.04-0.89), lower-body strength SMD 0.49 (0.01-0.98), no significant effect on upper-body strength, cycling sprint power, bench-press throw power or muscular endurance, and vertical jump SMD 0.36 only after excluding a low-quality study. The two in-record trials are approved without credit with their true directions: 30064450 (body fat down, squat/bench 1RM null) and 37409757 (more CrossFit repetitions, Wingate and body composition null). Proposed conclusion once the full text is read: a possible limited, outcome-scoped credit for lower-body maximal strength only, at the regimens the review reports; no cardiovascular, homocysteine or energy credit.

identity.standardization: Source Methods identifies Beta Power betaine; not betaine hydrochloride. No additional purity or chemical identifier inferred.

population.description: 23 young women (21.0 ± 1.4 y) without prior structured resistance training who completed the study (betaine n=11, placebo n=12); 13 dropouts/disqualifications reported.

study_contexts.study_design: Double-blind randomized placebo-controlled parallel trial; 1 week familiarization then 8 weeks supervised resistance training (3 sessions/week); groups matched for body composition and squat strength.

outcomes.name: Body fat percentage (a priori primary, power-calculated): greater decrease with betaine (-3.3 ± 1.7%) vs placebo (-1.7 ± 1.6%); fat mass -2.0 vs -0.8 kg (significant interactions)
Lean mass, rectus femoris thickness, vertical jump, squat and bench 1RM: no significant group-by-time interactions; weekly training volume trend p=0.056

limitations: Small sample of untrained young women during supervised resistance training; dietary intake suboptimal (Conclusions); no transfer to weight loss without training.
Betaine anhydrous (BetaPower); betaine HCl transfer rejected by Dr. Pham (A127).
